title: Discovery & Inventory Annex — Node Annotations and Health Heuristics
content:
Purpose:
This annex captures lightweight, operational-first conventions for how nodes advertise capabilities and health to the control plane and to downstream routers. It is intentionally pragmatic: small surface area, conservative TTLs, and deterministic health heuristics so routing decisions remain predictable across regions and failure modes.

Background / motivation:
We have several overlapping needs: a low-latency way for routers to pick a candidate node (or node pool) with the right GPU characteristics; an inventory that answers long-running queries (capacity, SKU mix) for planning/allocations; and a heartbeat stream that supports both fast failover and longer-term telemetry. Previous designs mixed detailed telemetry with discovery; that made routing brittle (too many signals, noisy) and inventory queries expensive. This doc prescribes a split: minimal live advertising (annotations + health score) plus richer async inventory records stored in the canonical inventory service.

Goals / constraints:
- Keep the discovery payload small (<= 1KB) for efficient broadcast/gossip and cross-region WAN.
- Provide enough compute characteristics so model->node compatibility matching is deterministic (no fuzzy guesses).
- Health score must be comparable across regions and stable under transient noise (avoid route flips on brief spikes).
- Make common policies expressible: exact-gpu-match, relaxed-compat (fallback to quantized model), latency-affinity, and cost-tier routing.
- Support both centralized control-plane reads (inventory queries, reconciliation) and decentralized fast routing decisions (local cache of annotations).

Inventory model (high level):
We maintain two complementary surfaces:
1) Live annotations (advertised via control-plane API and optional gossip): small, frequently updated, used by routers. Fields are node_id, zone/region, primary_gpu_tag, gpu_family, memory_gb, free_gpus, health_score, and versioned_capabilities (list of short strings).
2) Canonical inventory record (longer-lived, richer): contains full SKU, driver/kernel versions, installed libs (cuda/cudnn), quantization support flags, power/thermal profile, last_provisioned_at, and metadata for billing/ownership.

Why separate: routers need quick, compact answers. Inventory queries (who has these drivers; what is fleet distribution) are slower and heavier and belong behind the inventory service.

Node annotations vs labels (naming convention):
- label_*: used at provisioning time and written to canonical inventory (e.g., label_gpu_vendor=nvidia). These are authoritative and slow to change.
- ann_*: ephemeral annotations intended for fast advertising (e.g., ann_free_gpus=2, ann_temp_c=68). Routers should prefer ann_* when present.
- capability_*: short tokens controlled by runtime (e.g., capability_fp16, capability_4bit_q). Keep token set small and enumerated in/confluence.

GPU taxonomy (recommended annotation set):
- label_gpu_vendor (nvidia | amd | intel)
- label_gpu_model (A100-40GB | A100-80GB | H100 | RTX6000) — provisioning time
- ann_gpu_family (ampere | hopper | rdna2) — compact family for routing rules
- ann_gpu_mem_gb (integer) — allocatable memory in GB (rounded)
- ann_compute_cap (sm_80 | sm_86 | sm_90) — capability for kernel selection
- capability_fp16, capability_bf16, capability_4bit_q, capability_int8 (present/absent as tokens)

Health signals (what to advertise vs what to emit to telemetry):
Advertised (ann_):
- ann_health_score: 0-100 integer computed locally (see heuristic below). Routers use it to prefer nodes; any node < 30 is considered degraded for new allocations.
- ann_free_gpus: count of free GPU slots for immediate work (0..n)
- ann_pending_jobs: small count, helpful to avoid overcommitment
- ann_latency_ms_p50: median inference loop latency observed locally (short window) — optional for latency-first policies
- ann_heartbeat_ts: iso8601 timestamp. TTL for this annotation is 12s in local caches; if older, treat node as stale.
Telemetry (full): sent to telemetry pipeline and inventory service asynchronously
- detailed GPU utilization time-series, temperature trends, ECC errors, memory alloc failures, container crashes, oom_killer events, kernel versions, process maps.

Health score heuristic (local computation, deterministic):
Start with base 100, subtract weighted penalties (clamped 0..100):
- GPU memory pressure: - min(40, 2 * percentage_mem_in_use_above_threshold) [heavy weight]
- GPU temp > target (e.g., > 80C): - 10 for each 5C above threshold up to -30
- ECC or hardware error events in last 10m: -30 per event (cap -60)
- IO or RPC saturation (incoming queue length): - min(30, 2 * queue_len)
- Driver mismatch or unsupported model binary: -80 (hard fail)
- Successful probe liveness: +0 (no bonus)
Example: node with modest memory but a temp spike might be 100 - 20 - 10 = 70.
Rationale: we want a single scalar to drive ordering; keep heavy telemetry out of the score but surface severe errors as big penalties.

Control plane interactions / API contract (advertise pattern):
- POST /v1/nodes/register (id, zone, labels) — used at provisioning; idempotent.
- PUT /v1/nodes/:id/annotate (ann_payload) — frequent heartbeats/annotations with small payload; will update last_seen and ephemeral annotations. Payload size <1KB recommended.
- GET /v1/inventory/query?filter=... — full inventory queries (teams/tools).
- Event bus (Kafka) topic: node-annotations (compact updates) for consumers that want an event stream (routers optionally subscribe in-region).

Storage and consistency choices:
- Use strongly-consistent datastore for canonical inventory (for billing, reconciler).
- Use region-local caches with eventual replication for annotations. Router decision path must not depend on cross-region synchronous reads; prefer local cached annotations plus fallback to centralized inventory for non-latency paths.
- Annotations should include vector clock-ish monotonic timestamp to avoid regressions during reordering across networks.

Routing policies enabled by these signals:
- Exact-match: require label_gpu_model == requested_model && capability_fp16 present && ann_free_gpus > 0.
- Relaxed-match: prefer exact, else accept same family with capability_4bit_q (quantized fallback).
- Latency-affinity: prefer nodes with ann_latency_ms_p50 within X ms of the region median and ann_health_score >= Y.
- Cost-tier routing: nodes with label_billing_tier=spot vs reserved; routers can prefer cheaper pool when latency SLAs allow.
- Degraded avoidance: do not route to nodes with ann_health_score < 30 unless fallback pool is exhausted.

Multi-region considerations:
- Stale annotations: treat remote region annotations with stricter TTL (e.g., 6s) to reduce cross-region surprises. Only use cross-region nodes for new allocations when their ann_heartbeat_ts is within 6s and ann_latency_ms_p50 is within policy window.
- Capacity pools: maintain per-region aggregate view (region_free_gpus) in canonical inventory to make global placement decisions without reading every node.
- Failover / fallbacks: prefer in-region degraded nodes over healthy cross-region nodes when latency SLO is tight; otherwise prefer healthy remote capacity.
- Reconciliation: the inventory reconciler runs regional sweeps and generates corrective actions (taint node, mark for reprovision) if canonical inventory diverges from observed state for > 10m.

Operational playbook snippets (quick):
- Node flapping (health oscillates): increase local smoothing window from 10s to 60s for that node, mark for investigation if flapping persists > 30m.
- Silent nodes (no heartbeat > TTL*3): mark stale and drain; if still silent after 15m, mark as suspect-hardware and notify on-call.
- Thermal cluster event: if many nodes in a rack report temp penalties, escalate to infra to check CRACs and power.

Open decisions and TODOs:
- Enumerate canonical capability tokens (short list, company-wide). Confluence page linked above is the proposed set; need sign-off from Serving Runtime and Platform.
- Exact format for vector-clock timestamp in annotations (proposal: monotonic counter + ms epoch).
- Whether routers should subscribe to kafka topic directly or via control-plane fanout for simpler auth.

Appendix: short example annotation payload (plain text JSON for readability)
{
  "node_id": "node-az2-rc-12",
  "zone": "us-west-2a",
  "ann_gpu_family": "hopper",
  "ann_gpu_mem_gb": "80",
  "ann_free_gpus": "2",
  "capabilities": ["fp16","4bit_q"],
  "ann_health_score": "72",
  "ann_latency_ms_p50": "6",
  "ann_heartbeat_ts": "2025-11-02T15:04:03Z"
}

If you want, I can:
- produce a compact schema file (flat key list) for runtime engineers to implement annotate/advertise;
- generate a small simulator to compute health_score given sampled metrics for tuning penalties; or
- convert this into a short PRD for the Console team to surface region-level capacity in the UI.

Notes: keep this annex lightweight. The core property we want is predictable routing behavior in the face of noisy signals — fewer, well-chosen annotations are better than an avalanche of telemetry.
